claims.claim: Ant colonies are eusocial superorganisms, each housing queens, workers, and seasonal winged alates.
claims.evidence: Description of ant colonies as eusocial superorganisms
claims.quote: Ant colonies are eusocial, communal, and efficiently organized

claims.claim: The queen continuously lays eggs, which develop into larvae, then pupae, and finally into the various castes.
claims.evidence: Lack of explicit description of the queen's egg-laying process and caste development in the provided source material

claims.claim: Sterile workers tend the brood, forage for food, and maintain the nest, while soldiers defend it.
claims.quote: Typical colonies consist of various castes of sterile, wingless females, most of which are workers

claims.claim: When the colony matures, thousands of winged males and females—called alates—emerge and gather for a nuptial flight.
claims.evidence: Description of nuptial flights in ant colonies
claims.quote: Swarms of the winged sexuals (known as alates) depart the nest in search of other nests

claims.claim: During the flight, males mate briefly then die, while a few fertilized females land, shed their wings, and start new nests.
claims.evidence: Description of the fate of males and females after nuptial flights
claims.quote: The males die shortly thereafter, along with most of the females. A small percentage of the females survive to initiate new nests

claims.claim: These founding queens raise the first generation of workers alone, beginning the cycle anew.
claims.evidence: Lack of explicit description of the founding queen's role in raising the first generation of workers

claims.claim: Thus, from a single egg to a bustling metropolis, the ant colony’s life cycle repeats across the planet.
claims.evidence: Description of ant colonies and their life cycles
claims.quote: Ants have colonised almost every landmass on Earth
